summary: This document defines a YANG data model to manage IS-IS extensions for Segment Routing over the MPLS data plane. Operators can use it to configure and monitor those features in a vendor-neutral way.

eli5.summary: This is a standard settings form so operators can configure and monitor IS-IS segment routing on different vendors' routers.

questions: what is the is-is segment routing yang model
how to enable segment routing in is-is
subtitle: A standard YANG data model for configuring and monitoring IS-IS Segment Routing over MPLS.

tldr.problem: IS-IS has extensions for Segment Routing over MPLS, but there was no vendor-neutral YANG model to configure them or read their state through NETCONF or RESTCONF.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-isis-sr-mpls module augments the IS-IS model from RFC 9130 and reuses the base Segment Routing model from RFC 9020. It adds switches for SR, mapping server policy and TI-LFA, plus read-only views of the SR data in IS-IS LSPs.
tldr.outcome: Operators can manage IS-IS SR-MPLS the same way on any router that implements the module. It is a Proposed Standard published in December 2025.

today: RFC 9902 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2025. The metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Module Covers
sections.content:
RFC 9902 defines a device YANG data model that manages the IS-IS extensions for Segment Routing (SR) over the MPLS data plane. Those extensions are defined in RFC 8667. The model is an augmentation of the IS-IS YANG data model in RFC 9130, so it adds to the existing IS-IS tree instead of replacing it.

The document uses the graphical tree notation from RFC 8340 to show the model's structure.
sections.eli5: IS-IS is how routers learn the map of a network. This document adds a standard set of settings for the part of IS-IS that lets routers steer traffic along chosen paths.

sections.title: Design of the Module
sections.content:
The module, named ietf-isis-sr-mpls, depends on two others. It needs the base SR module from RFC 9020, which defines global SR management independent of any routing protocol, and the IS-IS base model from RFC 9130, which defines basic IS-IS configuration and state.

The module defines both the data nodes that configure IS-IS SR MPLS and the additions to the IS-IS Link State Protocol Data Units (LSPs) needed to support MPLS SR. It also imports types from several other RFCs, including the routing types of RFC 8294 and the routing model of RFC 8349.
sections.eli5: The new form is not built from scratch. It clips onto two existing forms, one for general segment routing and one for IS-IS, and adds the missing boxes.

sections.title: Activation and Mapping Server Policy
sections.content:
IS-IS SR MPLS is activated by setting an enabled leaf to true under the segment-routing container of the IS-IS instance. That triggers advertisement of the SR MPLS extensions, based on the parameters set up with the base SR module. The module also adds a per-protocol Segment Routing Global Block (protocol-srgb) when the base module's protocol-srgb feature is supported.

The base SR module defines mapping server policies. By default, IS-IS does not advertise or process any mapping server entry. The bindings/advertise/policies leaf-list lets IS-IS advertise one or more policies, and the bindings/receive leaf controls whether received mapping server entries are processed.

On each interface the module adds adjacency SID configuration. On a broadcast interface, each configured adjacency SID must also name a neighbor-system-id.
sections.eli5: There is one main switch that turns segment routing on. Another setting decides whether this router shares or listens to helper lists that give labels to places that cannot make their own.

sections.title: IP Fast Reroute with TI-LFA
sections.content:
The module augments the Fast Reroute (FRR) container under each IS-IS interface. It can activate Topology Independent Loop-Free Alternate (TI-LFA), using the ti-lfa feature, and it enhances Remote LFA (RLFA) so that it uses SR tunneling instead of LDP, using the remote-lfa-sr feature.

The TI-LFA container has an enabled leaf that defaults to false. Two optional tie-breakers choose between candidate backup paths: node-protection prefers a path that protects against the failure of the next node, and srlg-disjoint prefers a path that avoids links sharing a Shared Risk Link Group with the primary path. Each has a priority that defaults to 128, and a lower value is more preferred. TI-LFA enablement is also added at level-1 and level-2 of the LFA configuration.

For RLFA, the use-segment-routing-path leaf (default false) forces the SR path rather than the LDP path, and only takes effect when remote-lfa is enabled.
sections.eli5: If a road closes, a router needs a backup route ready. These settings turn on the smart backup-route feature and let you say which kind of backup you like best.

sections.title: Read-Only Views of IS-IS SR Data
sections.content:
Besides configuration, the module adds operational state. Per adjacency, a list of Adj-SIDs records the value, address family, weight and whether protection was requested.

In the IS-IS link state database it adds the SR data carried in advertisements: the router capability information (SR capability flags, global blocks, SR algorithms, SR Local Blocks and the SRMS preference, a value from 0 to 255 where 255 is most preferred), Adj-SID sub-TLVs on neighbors, Prefix-SID sub-TLVs on IPv4 and IPv6 reachability entries (including the multi-topology forms), and SID/Label Binding TLVs, including the multi-topology variant keyed by prefix and mt-id.

A SID can be given as a 20-bit MPLS label (range 0 to 1048575) or as a 32-bit index into a label space the router advertises. The module also defines flag identities for Prefix-SID, Adj-SID and SID binding sub-TLVs, taken from RFC 8667.
sections.eli5: As well as settings, the form has read-only boxes that show what other routers have announced, like a noticeboard of who offers which labels and paths.

sections.title: A Configuration Example
sections.content:
Appendix A gives the same example in XML and JSON. A router with ID 1.1.1.1 and IS-IS system ID 1111.2222.3333 has interface eth0 with an Adj-SID of 38888 toward neighbor 4444.5555.6666. SR is enabled for the IS-IS instance, and the protocol SRGB runs from a lower bound of 4000 to an upper bound of 5000.

Appendix B shows the full module tree.
sections.eli5: The example fills in the form for one router: turn segment routing on, give one link a special label, and pick a range of labels to use.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is meant to be accessed with YANG-based management protocols such as NETCONF and RESTCONF, which have to use a secure transport and mutual authentication. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM, RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

All writable nodes may be sensitive. Particularly sensitive subtrees are segment-routing and protocol-srgb under IS-IS, the interface segment-routing container, and the interface ti-lfa container. Disabling or changing SR configuration can cause a denial of service, because traffic may be dropped or misrouted.

Read access also matters: the router capability SR data and the augmentations to the IS-IS database can disclose operational state of IS-IS on a device. The document notes no particularly sensitive RPC or action operations.
sections.eli5: These settings steer a whole network, so only trusted people should be allowed to change or even look at them.
